Definition: from G3739 and G4169; of what kind that, i.e. how (as) great (excellent) (specially, as an indefinite correlative to the definite antecedent G5108 of quality):--what manner (sort) of, such as whatsoever.
BiblicalUsage: The word hopoîos is what manner (sort) of, such as whatsoever — a small word, used 5 times; Acts and 1 Corinthians show it in use.
TheologicalSignificance: My position is simple here: hopoîos means what manner (sort) of, such as whatsoever, and I do not stretch it further.
RelatedEvents: Paul Before Felix, Festus, and Agrippa
